**My thinking:**

I have about 10 mu of land that my family has farmed for years here in Quzhou. Everyone around me grows winter wheat and summer maize — one after the other on the same land. That's what I know how to do, that's what the local supply shops sell seeds and fertilizer for, and that's what the grain buyers will come to collect. I'm not going to try anything different. My neighbor tried vegetables a few years back and had trouble finding buyers — I don't want that risk.

For seeds, I buy from the village supply station. They sell the improved seeds that the county recommends. Not the fanciest hybrid, but better than saving my own — I learned that lesson when yields dropped.

I apply compound fertilizer when I plant, then add urea when the wheat is jointing. My brother-in-law told me this is what gets the yield up. I don't have a soil test — I just follow the same amounts as last year because the yields were acceptable.

I irrigate wheat three or four times. The well pump costs money but skipping water in spring means lost grain. For maize, the summer rains usually help so I irrigate less.

I spray herbicide after wheat emerges and spray again before harvest for disease. For maize I spray herbicide early and watch for pests.
